claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from first-cohort volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group; 162 samples in total) across the study time points, using linear mixed models with contrasts versus baseline, false discovery rate adjustment, and a fold-change >2 cutoff, showed that a robust set of 239 transcripts was significantly altered in response to vaccination compared to the average of the two baseline time points.

sources.quote: Specific time points where significant differences were found in comparison to baseline for each group (false discovery rate [FDR] = 0.10) were identified. Of the 3,102 transcripts for which abundance was significantly altered in response to vaccines, 239 changed by more than 2-fold in at least one time point.

Figure 1 Blood Transcriptional Profiles of Vaccinated Subjects(A) Patterns of changes in transcript abundance are shown on a heatmap for a robust set of 239 transcripts using an FDR of 0.10 and fold change >2). For each subject, data are normalized to the average of the two baseline time points.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from first-cohort volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group; 162 samples in total) across the study time points, using linear mixed models with contrasts versus baseline and false discovery rate adjustment, showed that the number of responsive genes was largest in the pneumococcal vaccine group compared to the influenza vaccine and saline control groups.

sources.quote: It is thus possible to visualize that the number of responsive genes was the largest for the pneumococcal vaccine group and the smallest for the saline control group.

(B) Lists of genes differentially expressed in response to each treatment for all time points or at each time point for all treatments are represented as segments on a circle. The length of the segments is proportional to the number of genes in each list.
